anti_overlap: Do not analyze the architecture of a single encounter or its ceremonial weight — that is the chanoyu lens
Do not analyze lure-mechanic reciprocity or creature time — that is the falconry lens
Do not analyze the ethics of intentional unharvested edges — that is the gleaning lens (related but distinct: gleaning is about deliberate non-harvest; foraging is about real-world scarcity)
Focus only on encounter distribution shape across a walk and the legitimacy of the empty session
decision_lens: Does this density option produce an honest distribution curve that respects 'nothing today' as a real outcome, or does it engineer-out the empty walks that give the full ones their meaning?
distance_rationale: A subsistence-and-pleasure practice from non-Western and Nordic folk traditions with documented real-world distribution curves of finds — provides empirical ground-truth for what an 'honest' walk-find density curve looks like in a non-engineered system
expected_isomorphisms: Find distribution per kilometer of forest walk maps directly to Unc encounter distribution per kilometer; the legitimacy of zero-find walks maps to whether Option D's possible-zero outcome is correct; patch knowledge maps to whether locations should weakly remember prior encounters; season/weather dependency maps to whether real-world conditions should modulate Unc availability; the ethic of restraint maps to game-design choices about over-luring
focus: The actual density curve of a forest walk, when nothing-today is correct, the ethics of returning to known patches
name: fd-mushroom-foraging-encounter-distribution
persona: Apply the perspective of a traditional Northern-European mushroom forager in the Finnish/Swedish/Polish 'everyman's right' (allemansrätten) tradition — they care about the real distribution of finds across a walk (which is bursty and patchy, not uniform), the legitimacy of 'nothing today,' the ethics of returning to known patches, and the way the empty walk is part of the practice not a failure mode.
review_areas: Whether Option D's 50%/90% probability curve resembles real mushroom-walk distributions (it is closer than Options A/B/C, but real distributions are patchier still — multi-find clusters separated by empty stretches)
Whether Option A's guarantee eliminates the foraging-walk's central truth: sometimes the forest gives nothing and that is correct
Whether Option C's '~1 per km capped at 3-4' produces a uniform distribution that no real-world walk produces (real walks are 0,0,0,3,0,0,1 not 1,1,1,1)
Whether the game should support 'patch knowledge' — Uncs encountered before in specific places have higher re-encounter rates, like a known chanterelle spot
Whether season/weather/time-of-day modulation (foraging's core dependencies) should ever shape Unc-availability, or whether that violates the lure-driven design
Whether re-luring with the same media within a short window should produce diminishing returns the way over-picked patches do

severity_examples.condition: Eliminating zero-find walks removes the cognitive contrast that makes finds meaningful; foraging research and folk-knowledge both confirm that the empty walk is not a bug but a load-bearing element of the practice
Uniform density across a walk produces an unnaturally flat experience curve; real foraging distributions are bursty and patchy, which is what makes the walk interesting to attentive walkers
If a player returns to a place where they previously encountered an Unc, the game should weakly remember this — not deterministically, but in the way a forager remembers their patches

source_domain: Northern-European mushroom foraging in the allemansrätten tradition — Finnish, Swedish, and Polish folk practices documented in field studies and mycological survey data
success_hints: Argue from real distribution data: foraging walks are bursty/patchy, not Poisson and not uniform
Defend the empty walk explicitly — name it a load-bearing design element, not a churn risk
Distinguish 'rare event' (low-probability per unit time, can happen anywhere) from 'patchy event' (clustered in space and time) — Option D conflates them
Note that allemansrätten encodes an ethic of restraint: foragers leave young mushrooms and don't strip patches — what is the Unc Rancher equivalent?
task_context: Review encounter-density options A/B/C/D for Unc Rancher v0 through the lens of real foraging-walk distributions and the legitimacy of the empty walk.
